html:
Boethuk is this map's spelling of Beothuk, the Indigenous people of Newfoundland. For the years 1000 to 1200 it marks their ancestors on the island.

Archaeologists call the people of these centuries the Little Passage complex. They hunted caribou inland and took seals, fish and birds on the coast, much as the later Beothuk did, and are seen as their direct ancestors. They lived on the island at the time of the Norse camp at L'Anse aux Meadows, around 1021, on Newfoundland's northern tip, and they may be among the people the Norse sagas call Skraelings. Their neighbours on the mainland were the ancestors of the Innu.
sum: Boethuk is this map's spelling of Beothuk, the Indigenous people of Newfoundland. For the years 1000 to 1200 it marks their ancestors on the island.
